messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 26-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after threatening to harm his roommate earlier today. He reports that someone on the radio told him to do so. His family reports that, during the past two years, the patient has become increasingly more withdrawn from family and friends. He states that he has spent the majority of the last year alone in his room “working on a project at home to save the earth from an evil alien power.” There is no family history of serious illness. He has smoked marijuana on a daily basis since he was thirteen. Vital signs are within normal limits. On mental status examination, he has a flat affect and his speech is disorganized. An MRI scan of the head is most likely to show which of the following?

Options:
A. Periventricular plaques and white matter lesions
B. Nucleus caudatus atrophy
C. Ring-enhancing lesion
D. Hyperintense temporal lobe lesion
E. Enlarged cerebral ventricles

Correct answer: E. Enlarged cerebral ventricles

text: {"psychiatry": true, "dsm_answerable": true, "category": "diagnosis", "reason": "The vignette depicts schizophrenia, and DSM-5's associated features note neuroimaging findings such as ventricular enlargement, making the answer derivable from DSM-5."}
